title: Invoices go out incomplete
blurb: The invoice a customer receives can be missing their address, tax ID and payment terms, and quantities can print blank. Bills raised this way never show as overdue, so nothing chases them.

title: Payments are recorded by hand, and foreign currency is guessed
blurb: Settling an invoice means retyping figures outside the system, and a payment in another currency posts a gain or loss that never happened.

title: Quotes can go out under-priced
blurb: The agreed rate card is not always enforced when a quotation is priced, so a job can be sold below the rate the customer was promised.

title: Approvals do not hold
blurb: A quotation, order or fee can be changed after it is submitted or approved, so what a manager signed off is not always what ships. One person can also approve their own work.

title: Shipping documents can be released without the right checks
blurb: A bill of lading can be marked released or held without going through release control, can be rewritten while under review, and scanned values are accepted without flagging what failed validation.

title: Enquiries that do not arrive by email leave no record
blurb: WhatsApp, phone, walk-in and agent enquiries are not recorded, so win rate cannot be measured. A quotation's date and salesperson are stamped automatically and cannot be corrected, and a wrongly recorded win or loss is permanent.

title: Customer records duplicate, and credit limits are not checked
blurb: The same customer can exist twice under different spellings, splitting their history. Credit limits are recorded but never consulted when invoicing, and a customer with contacts on file can still have nobody to chase.

title: Jobs lose their number, and paperwork cannot be filed against them
blurb: A job created from a won quotation starts without a job number, documents cannot be attached to the job they belong to, nothing enforces what a job must contain, and the intake queue is a dead end.

title: Tracking and haulage sit apart from the job
blurb: Customs and port tracking cannot be seen from the shipment it belongs to, the customs declaration itself lives outside the system, trucks are not linked to jobs, and a shipment can never be closed.

title: Month-end figures cannot be trusted at a glance
blurb: One shipment can report two different profit figures, and the month-end documents are hidden inside an export dialog rather than being where month-end work happens.
